FULL.notes:
[chunk 1/3] ORACLE Q1 FY2026 (10-Q, filed 2025-09-10): Extraction focused on SIFI-material relationships, capex commitments, and off-balance-sheet obligations. KEY FINDINGS: (1) AMPERE CIRCULARITY: Oracle holds 29% equity in Ampere Computing (equity method, $1.7B carrying value) plus convertible debt maturing June 2026. SoftBank announced acquisition of Ampere (announced March 2025, pending closing). Oracle also holds call/put options at $0.5B-$1.5B prices through Jan 2027. This creates a three-way investor-supplier circularity with exit uncertainty tied to SoftBank's timing. (2) CAPEX-ROI GAP: Oracle deployed $8.5B capex in Q1 (3-month run-rate ~$34B annualized). Simultaneously, Oracle committed to $99.8B in operating lease obligations for data centers (10-16 year terms, commencing FY2026-FY2028) PLUS $6.6B subsequent commitment (announced post-filing, FY2027-FY2028 start). These are UNCOMMITTED leases—not yet on balance sheet as of 8/31/25. No disclosed customer prepayments or multi-year cloud contracts matching this scale. (3) EXECUTION RISK: Data center commitments span 10-16 years with staggered commencement; capex line item shows depreciation $1.35B Q1, suggesting aggressive infrastructure expansion without visible matched revenue contracts in forward guidance. (4) FINANCE LEASE EMERGENCE: Q1 shows first-ever finance lease cost ($107M, split $59M amortization + $48M interest), rising from $0 in prior year, suggesting new lease-financing arrangements. Operating lease ROU assets jumped 22% Q-o-Q ($13.1B→$15.9B), indicating significant new lease portfolio. (5) AMPERE INVESTMENT TRACKING: Oracle states it will recognize "share of loss" in Ampere until SoftBank acquisition closes; no timeline given. Ampere appears to be unprofitable (reflected in equity method losses). Oracle's equity method accounting masks the underlying operational deterioration. Convertible debt maturity (June 2026, ~1 yr) creates forced resolution/refinancing event. (6) REMAINING PERFORMANCE OBLIGATIONS: $455.3B as of 8/31/25, but only ~10% expected to recognize in next 12 months; 25% in months 13-36; 34% in months 37-60. This backlog is long-dated and subject to renewal risk (forward-looking statement notes "expectation that substantially all of our customers will renew their software support contracts upon expiration"—a subjective caveat). No customer concentration disclosure provided in this excerpt, but cloud revenue only $7.2B vs. total revenue $14.9B (~48%), suggesting Oracle cloud business is still maturing vs. legacy software. No named counterparty cloud contracts disclosed (e.g., no mention of OpenAI, Google, Amazon, Microsoft commitments as customers or infrastructure partners).
[chunk 2/3] EXTRACTION SUMMARY: Oracle 10-Q (Q1 FY2026, filed 2025-09-10). SOURCE TEXT focused on financial narrative: Item 7 (Income Taxes), Note 8 (Segment Information), Item 9 (EPS), Item 10 (Legal Proceedings), and Item 2 (MD&A Business Overview). SIFI-MATERIAL FINDINGS: (1) AMPERE COMPUTING INVESTMENT: Oracle holds 29% equity stake (carrying value $1.7B) plus convertible debt ($90M in Q1 FY2026). This is a material portfolio holding but disclosed as an equity method investment. (2) EXECUTION_RISK flagged: Pending SoftBank acquisition of Ampere (announced 2025-03-19) creates liquidity uncertainty. Oracle's investment subject to closure contingencies and potential loss recognition until deal closes. Severity 2 (concern) — material but not single-point-of-failure. (3) INTERNATIONAL TAX LITIGATION: Oracle disclosed significant tax audits/litigation in 12+ jurisdictions (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, S. Korea, Spain). Amounts "significant" but no materiality statement on financial impact. Severity 2. (4) DEFERRED TAX ASSET REALIZATION: $9.8B net deferred tax asset carries realization risk dependent on future taxable income. Standard language but disclosed. Severity 1 (watch). NO OTHER SIFI-MATERIAL ENTITIES OR RELATIONSHIPS identified in this excerpt. The filing discusses routine business segments (cloud/software 86% of revenue, hardware 5%, services 9%), standard geographic revenue mix, and ordinary restructuring/stock-based comp charges. No hidden leverage, circularity, revenue roundtripping, capex commitments to strategic counterparties, customer/supplier concentration > 10%, or off-balance-sheet structures were disclosed. The Ampere investment is the key SIFI signal — it represents a material portfolio stake in an AI-adjacent infrastructure company whose exit timeline is now controlled by SoftBank.
[chunk 3/3] EXTRACTION SUMMARY — Oracle 10-Q Q1 FY2026 (filed 2025-09-10):

KEY SIFI SIGNALS EXTRACTED:

1. **CAPEX_ROI_GAP (Severity 3)**: Oracle's trailing-12-month capex surged to $27.4B (+249% YoY) while operating cash flow grew only 13% to $21.5B, resulting in negative free cash flow of -$5.9B. The majority of capex funds 'second-generation cloud infrastructure' development with no disclosed contracted customer revenue matching the investment scale. This represents a classic CAPEX_ROI_GAP pattern typical of hyperscaler cloud-build wars.

2. **EXECUTION_RISK (Severity 3)**: Oracle is restructuring operations and reallocating cost savings to fund unproven cloud infrastructure. The filing discloses investments in 'development and delivery of our second-generation cloud infrastructure' but provides no detail on operational readiness, customer pre-commitments, or timeline. This is typical execution risk for greenfield cloud infrastructure projects.

3. **CUSTOMER_CONCENTRATION (Severity 3)**: Remaining performance obligations (RPO) jumped 359% from $99.1B (Aug 2024) to $455.3B (Aug 2025). The filing explicitly states this increase was driven by 'certain significant cloud contracts' but does NOT disclose:
   - Customer identity (hyperscaler? tech giant? government?)
   - Number of customers
   - Revenue concentration (% of total RPO)
   - Contract terms or termination risk
   This opacity around 'significant' cloud contracts is material to SIFI analysis, especially given the cloud infrastructure space concentration around NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta.

4. **EQUITY METHOD INVESTMENT — Ampere**: Oracle holds an equity method investment in Ampere Computing (a CPU/AI chip design firm). The filing indicates Oracle is taking losses on this investment. Ampere is a known competitor to NVIDIA in the server CPU space and a supplier to Oracle's second-gen cloud infrastructure plans. This represents a potential circular dependency (Oracle funding a cloud CPU supplier while also competing with hyperscalers who use NVIDIA).

OTHER OBSERVATIONS (NOT EXTRACTED — BOILERPLATE):
- Restructuring expenses of $402M (related to cloud/infrastructure shift).
- Interest expense up 10% to $923M (higher debt from $14B bond issuance in FY2025).
- Cloud segment margins are healthy (67% for cloud/SaaS), but absolute growth is slowing.
- Lease commitments increased "substantially all for data centers" with additional commitments post-period, but no quantification provided.
- Tax provision jumped 108% due to "One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act" deferred tax remeasurement, not operational.

NODES NOT EXTRACTED:
- Specific cloud customers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) — none named in this excerpt.
- Data center counterparties (CoreWeave, Lambda, or other infrastructure partners) — none named.
- Brookfield, Blue Owl, or other off-balance-sheet financing structures — none disclosed in this section.
- Other investees beyond Ampere — this excerpt does not detail NVIDIA's or Oracle's other portfolio holdings mentioned in Note 8.

RECOMMENDATION FOR DOWNSTREAM ANALYSIS:
Review Oracle's Note 8 (Non-marketable Equity Securities) in the full 10-K/10-Q to enumerate all investees and identify circular dependencies with cloud infrastructure vendors and AI labs.
